notes: Access: standard Shopify storefront, robots.txt has no ClaudeBot-specific disallow (generic Shopify bot-notice only); direct fetch worked for most pages but the site's Cloudflare layer 429'd repeated plain-requests fetches mid-session, so all products.json pagination was done via curl_cffi impersonate='chrome124' thereafter (Rule 2 step 2). housedoctor.com is a MULTI-BRAND Shopify storefront: House Doctor's own furnishing/decor line plus two sister brands sold on the same domain -- Meraki (wellness/home-fragrance/personal care) and Nicolas Vahe (gourmet food) -- both entirely out of scope per the Home Fragrance / food-consumables / personal-care exclusions, and excluded here (their collections dominate the raw /collections.json listing of 264 handles but are not part of this extraction). Scope was taken from the site's own English 'Products' mega-menu (House Doctor's type-tree navigation) under the /en-int locale. RULE 1 (qty verification): Shopify's products_count field (surfaced by /collections.json) was confirmed inflated on every single category checked here -- e.g. 'Candles & LED candles' reported 25 but exhaustively paginating /collections/<handle>/products.json by unique product ID yields only 2; 'Decorative items' reported 90 vs 53 actual; 'Tealight holders & candle holders' reported 199 vs 87 actual. Every qty in this file is the exhaustive unique-product-ID count from products.json pagination (limit=250; every collection here fit on a single page, confirming exhaustion), never the raw products_count field. RULE 0.6 (type tree + room tree): the site also has a 'Rooms' mega-menu (Entrance, Kitchen, Dining area, Living room, Bathroom, Bedroom, Wardrobe) layered over the SAME underlying Shopify collections. Verified empirically via product-ID overlap: 'Entrance lighting' (122 raw) is 110/122 identical products to the union of the Lighting type-tree subcategories already counted here, with the other 12 being bulbs/sockets/cords (excluded category anyway) -- dropped as a duplicate rollup. 'Bedroom lighting' (58) and 'Dining table lamps' (30) are both 100% subsets of the same Lighting type-tree union -- dropped as pure re-cuts. The room-tree 'Kitchen'/'Dining area'/'Living room'/'Bathroom'/'Bedroom'/'Wardrobe'/'Entrance' top-level room collections (627-1619 raw items each) are mixed roll-ups spanning furniture+textiles+decor+storage for that room -- dropped per 'mixed roll-ups: drop, don't pad'; their submenus were inspected and every sub-item is either an exact-URL duplicate of an already-counted type-tree node or an already-excluded type (storage/textiles/furniture). One genuinely NEW room-tree node survived: the room-scoped 'Mirrors' collection (handle 'mirrors', 3 products, all Meraki-branded compact/vanity mirrors, 0% product-ID overlap with the type-tree 'Mirrors' handle 'mirrors-1', 25 products, all House-Doctor-branded) -- kept as a second Mirrors row per Rule 0.3 (all mirrors in scope) since it is a genuinely distinct, non-duplicate product set. Another room-tree-only node, 'Tableware' (handle 'tableware', 231 raw), was inspected by title and found to be a mixed roll-up superset of the already-counted Plates & Bowls/Glasses,Mugs & Cups/Carafes & Jugs PLUS substantial excluded content (cutlery, placemats, napkins, chopping boards, picnic cooler bags) -- dropped per 'mixed roll-ups: drop, don't pad', keeping the three cleaner type-tree tableware subcategories instead. OTHER EXCLUSION-BY-TITLE-INSPECTION calls: 'Outdoor decor' (handle 'outdoor-decor', 10 products) inspected by title and found to be 100% parasols/cushions/throws -- i.e. outdoor furniture and textiles despite the 'decor' name -- dropped entirely (product type beats category label in both directions). 'Chopping boards & serving' (26 products) is a mixed cookware(chopping boards)+serveware roll-up -- dropped. 'Bathroom accessories' (handle 'bathroom-accessories-1', 65 products) inspected by title and found to be almost entirely functional fixtures/storage (toilet brushes, soap dispensers, toothbrush holders, trash cans, laundry baskets/bags, toilet-paper holders, towel holders, hooks, shelves) rather than decorative items -- dropped per bathroom furniture/storage/fixtures exclusion. 'Home Office > Accessories' (handle 'tilbehor', 2 products) is tablet/laptop sleeves -- excluded. 'Racks, Hangers & Hooks' (handle 'racks-hangers-hooks', 46 products, filed under the site's own 'Storage' menu branch) was kept IN SCOPE per Rule 0's explicit 'decorative metal ... hooks, racks' inclusion -- titles are dominated by wall hooks ('Knage', many in decorative colours) and hook rails ('Knagerakke'), with a handful of functional wire hangers/clothes-stands mixed in that were not stripped out individually. Standard exclusions applied without further comment: Furniture (all), Home Textiles (all: cushion covers/filling, throws, rugs, door mats), Storage (bags/purses/shoppers, knobs & handles, bins, kitchen/bathroom storage, laundry baskets), Kitchen (cutlery, cocktail/bar accessories, kitchen storage, kitchen textiles, place mats, napkins), Bulbs/cords/sockets, Outdoor furniture/textiles, Home Office (storage/paper/office supplies), Wardrobe baskets. 'Home Decor' (handle 'home-decor', parent) and 'Kitchen accessories' (parent) are the site's own umbrella/rollup collections whose product counts approximately sum their children -- not extracted as their own leaf rows, used only as parent hierarchy labels. No duplicate-company flag applies to S.N. 176 (no prior House Doctor extraction in this project).
